title: Return from authorized Investigate Case Timeline and source to the originally selected Command Incident
goal: Close CAP-CMD-106 §17/§25 Class-0 Incident→Investigate→Incident navigation in the already runnable first-party local browser, without creating an authorization bridge, mutation, redirect, source store, new route or paid API.
invariants: The Command Incident ID originates in a Command-authorized selected Incident link, but after HTTP roundtrips is UNTRUSTED presentation-only navigation data; it does not authorize Case, Timeline Entry or source read.
Case Timeline keeps checking its own trusted host session, Case, Timeline Entry and typed source owner on EVERY read; source preview independently checks owner.read and the source object identity.
Returning to /command/work-queue?view=incidents&selected=Incident:... triggers the existing Command session and owner read checks; no permission or scope transferred from Investigate.
Accept origin_incident ONLY on explicit text/html Case Timeline requests, absent from JSON legacy API and all permission/tenant/source owner query selection.
Source return_to URL allows only same Case /case-timeline path with one strictly bounded optional incident ID; no host, scheme, fragment, duplicate keys or extra permissions.
The link is fixed same-origin path constructed with url.Values; no arbitrary external URL, redirect, referer credential, raw sourceRef or inherited owner decision.
Preserve prior selection/pagination filters and synthetic local browser behavior without modifying prior review SHA #206 or any parent.
security_properties: invalid origin UTF8/control/whitespace/empty/multivalue/over128 and any owner-scope query parameter rejected before Case/source presentation
Replay of navigation on commander-only principal grants only previously independently authorized Command Incident, never Case or source
No effect to JSON API, source JSON, existing historic local Case/browser links without origin, raw source availability or original partial/unknown Timeline states

migration.rationale: Only optional HTML navigation query and links; no stored schema or mutable data
